title: Add generate orchestration error-branch tests (Render/Lock/Verify/Fsx/generic exceptions)
description:
src/python_foundry/generate/orchestrate.py:174-212 handles PlanBindError, RenderError, LockError, VerifyError, FsxError, and generic Exception, wrapping each into GenerateError with the right error_class and stage_path. Only the PlanBindError branch is currently tested (test_generate.py lines ~47-59). Lines 53-54 (symlink preservation during artifact purge) and 114-123 are also uncovered.

Add tests for each remaining branch, using real fixtures (not mocks) where feasible:
- RenderError path: plan referencing a missing/corrupt catalog source -> GenerateError error_class='render', stage_path set and absolute, stage preserved on disk for inspection
- LockError path: stage with an unsatisfiable/invalid dependency in pyproject.toml -> GenerateError error_class='lock', stage preserved, destination untouched
- VerifyError path: generated content with a real ruff/ty failure (reuse fixtures from the verify/runners.py test work) -> GenerateError error_class='verify', stage preserved, destination untouched (fail-closed guarantee)
- FsxError path: destination whose parent is not a directory -> GenerateError error_class='fsx' (or matching taxonomy), before any stage write side effects leak
- Generic Exception path: confirm it's wrapped as error_class='internal' (or documented equivalent) rather than propagating raw
- _purge_build_artifacts symlink preservation: create a stage with a symlink under .venv, run purge, assert symlink still exists afterward (orchestrate.py:53-54)
- Confirm .venv/__pycache__/.ruff_cache/.pytest_cache/*.egg-info are absent from the destination after a successful generate+place (purge-before-place behavior)

For every failure case, explicitly assert: (a) destination directory is NOT created/modified, (b) stage_path in the error is absolute and still exists on disk (unless the error occurs pre-stage).
acceptance_criteria: One test per bullet, each asserting error_class + stage-preserved/destination-untouched invariants; orchestrate.py lines 53-54,114-123,174-212 coverage closed.

title: Add catalog integrity failure tests (missing versions.toml, manifest id/kind mismatch, missing core/cli units)
description:
src/python_foundry/catalog/load.py has multiple integrity checks that are completely untested (coverage gaps at lines 138-142, 146, 151, 182-183, 189, 197, 202, 207, 214, 221, 228, 241, 259, 265, 271, 277, 283, 301-320, 330-331, 339, 346-347). These enforce catalog integrity (a corrupted catalog could currently load silently or fail with the wrong error).

Using tmp_path-built fake catalog trees (versions.toml + core/manifest.toml + archetype/cli/manifest.toml as a base), add tests for:
- missing versions.toml -> CatalogLoadError code catalog.missing_versions (or actual code name, verify from source)
- missing core unit -> code catalog.missing_core
- missing archetype/cli unit -> code catalog.missing_cli
- manifest.toml with invalid TOML syntax -> code catalog.manifest_toml
- manifest.toml root is an array, not a table -> code catalog.manifest_root
- manifest id field doesn't match its directory-derived expected id -> code catalog.manifest_id
- manifest kind field doesn't match expected kind, or is an invalid kind value -> code catalog.manifest_kind
- description field non-string -> code catalog.manifest_description
- apply_order non-int -> code catalog.manifest_order
- files field not an array -> code catalog.manifest_files
- dependencies not an array, or containing empty/non-string entries -> code catalog.manifest_dependencies
- a [[files]] entry that is not a table -> code catalog.file_entry
- a [[files]] entry missing path/render/source or with an empty path -> code catalog.file_entry
- render field not one of static|template -> code catalog.file_render
- mode field non-string, override field non-bool -> appropriate codes
- Catalog.show('') / Catalog.show('   ') -> code catalog.empty_ref

Read the exact error codes/messages from catalog/load.py and catalog/errors.py rather than guessing; assert both .code and .error_class on each.
acceptance_criteria: Each bullet has a corresponding passing test with a real assertion on error code/class; catalog/load.py coverage gap lines closed (or reduced to only unreachable defensive lines).

title: Add real tool-failure tests for verify/runners.py (ruff/ty/pytest never actually triggered)
description:
src/python_foundry/verify/runners.py:23-27,76,80,93-94 are uncovered. tests/test_verify_runners.py only exercises the 'none' mode skip path and a constant string. The actual failure path (raising VerifyError on nonzero subprocess exit) is NEVER exercised with real failing input -- meaning verify tiers are unproven to actually catch a lint error, type error, or failing test.

Add tests using real generated stages (via existing generate()/render helpers) with deliberately broken content:
- default mode: inject a file with a ruff lint violation (e.g. unused import) -> VerifyError raised with code containing 'ruff_check', message includes ruff output
- default mode: inject a file with a ty type error -> VerifyError with code containing 'ty_check'
- strict mode: inject a failing pytest test -> VerifyError with code containing 'pytest', and confirm strict mode's step list includes pytest (runners.py:76) while default's does not
- skip_network_tools=True excludes uv_sync_locked from steps_run (runners.py:80)
- default mode steps_run == exactly the expected 4-tuple (uv_sync_locked, ruff_check, ruff_format_check, ty_check) -- pin this as a regression guard
- VerifyError fields (message, code, stage_path, verify_mode) are populated correctly (runners.py:23-27)

These should use real subprocess execution (uv/ruff/ty/pytest), consistent with the existing trustworthy pattern in test_spk001_smoke.py, not mocks.
acceptance_criteria: At least one test per bullet above passes and fails if the corresponding runners.py logic is reverted/broken. verify/runners.py coverage of lines 23-27,76,80,93-94 closed.

title: Add tests for hybrid/__main__.py (0% coverage) - public template CI drift gate
description:
hybrid/__main__.py (lines 3-76, entirely uncovered) is the CLI entrypoint run in CI to detect drift between the catalog and the frozen public GitHub template (python-foundry-template). It has zero tests: arg parsing (--spec/--golden/--work-dir/--skip-verify), default paths, temp-dir lifecycle, exit codes on match/drift, and error message formatting are all unverified. If this silently breaks, the public template can drift from the catalog without CI catching it.

New file tests/test_hybrid_main.py, invoking the module as a real subprocess (uv run python -m python_foundry.hybrid ...):
- exits 0 when golden matches regenerated snapshot (examples/python-foundry-template.toml vs tests/goldens/hybrid-python-foundry-template)
- exits nonzero and prints drift info when golden is deliberately corrupted (copy golden, mutate one file, point --golden at the copy)
- --skip-verify flag is accepted and uv.lock is still produced in the work dir
- missing --spec path produces a nonzero exit with a clear error message
- missing --golden dir produces a nonzero exit with a clear error message
- default invocation (no --spec/--golden args) resolves to the real defaults and passes in a clean checkout

Acceptance: hybrid/__main__.py coverage >0% and all listed scenarios covered; CI still green.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_hybrid_main.py exists and covers: match/exit0, drift/exit-nonzero, --skip-verify, missing spec, missing golden, default args. hybrid/__main__.py no longer at 0% coverage.

title: Fix dead 'unknown keys hard-fail' test in test_spec.py:150
description:
tests/test_spec.py around line 150 has an 'if False else' guard around the _minimal(extra_key=...) parametrize case, so the case testing spec's hard-fail-on-unknown-keys requirement never actually executes. This is the primary regression test for a headline spec requirement (docs/02-definitive-specification-revised.md: 'TOML schema=1; non-interactive; hard-fail unknown keys/profiles') and it is currently dead code.

Fix: remove the dead branch, make the parametrize case actually call _minimal(unknown_key="nope") (or equivalent), and assert SpecValidationError / SpecParseError is raised with the correct code (e.g. spec.unknown_key) and error_class == 'validation'. Add a second case for an unknown key nested under [profiles] or other subtables if the schema supports nested tables, to ensure the hard-fail is not only top-level.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown-key case is live (no dead code), asserts on the correct error code/class, and fails against a version of spec/validate.py that doesn't reject unknown keys (verified by temporarily reverting the check).

title: Add generate/lock.py failure-path tests (missing pyproject, uv lock failure, missing artifact)
description:
src/python_foundry/generate/lock.py:19-22,30,43-44,51 are uncovered: LockError __init__ fields, missing pyproject.toml (code lock.missing_pyproject), nonzero uv lock subprocess exit (code lock.uv_failed, stderr truncated to 500 chars per source), and uv lock succeeding but uv.lock file not appearing (code lock.missing_artifact).

Add tests:
- produce_uv_lock() on a stage dir with no pyproject.toml -> LockError code lock.missing_pyproject, stage_path set
- produce_uv_lock() on a stage with a pyproject.toml declaring an unsatisfiable/nonexistent dependency (e.g. a made-up package name+version) -> real 'uv lock' subprocess actually fails -> LockError code lock.uv_failed, message/detail includes truncated stderr
- for the lock.missing_artifact branch (uv succeeds but file absent), it's acceptable to monkeypatch subprocess.run to return code 0 without writing the file, since faking a genuine uv bug is impractical -> assert LockError code lock.missing_artifact
- LockError fields (message, code, stage_path) populated correctly
Also from the broader audit: verify idempotent/deterministic lock production -- running generate twice against the same spec/catalog produces byte-identical uv.lock, and changing a pinned dependency version changes the lock (regression guard for 'generate produces/refreshes uv.lock to match resolution').
acceptance_criteria: Each bullet has a passing test with real subprocess uv calls where feasible; generate/lock.py coverage gap lines closed.

title: Add fsx stage/place error-path tests (collision exhaustion, non-directory parent, missing-stage, symlink dest)
description:
src/python_foundry/fsx has several untested error paths: stage.py:80-84 (stage_parent: destination parent missing/not-a-directory), stage.py:97-101 (generic OSError during create, non-collision), stage.py:111-115 (fsx.stage_exhausted after MAX_STAGE_CREATE_ATTEMPTS collisions), place.py:51-56 (fsx.place_stage_missing when stage.path no longer exists at place time), place.py:67-86 (cross-device rename fallback to copytree, and cleanup on copytree failure), place.py:18 (destination_is_nonempty when destination is a symlink to an empty vs non-empty dir), paths.py:31-36 (Path.is_absolute() catches platform-specific absolute forms like a Windows-style path even on POSIX), paths.py:50-56 (is_within_stage helper has zero callers in tests), errors.py:24/37 (__str__ methods).

Add targeted unit tests for each, e.g.:
- create_stage() against a destination path whose parent is a file, not a directory -> StageError code fsx.stage_parent
- create_stage() with a token factory that always returns the same colliding token for 16+ calls -> StageError code fsx.stage_exhausted, message includes last_err
- exclusive_place() given a Stage whose .path was deleted after creation -> PlaceError code fsx.place_stage_missing
- destination_is_nonempty() on a symlink pointing to an empty dir vs a dir with files
- confine_path() rejects a value that only Path.is_absolute() (not raw '/'/'\\' prefix check) would catch
- is_within_stage() direct unit tests: path inside stage, path outside stage, boundary/equal path
- str(StageError('msg')) == 'msg' and same for PlaceError
Cross-device rename failure is acceptable to skip if it can't be reliably simulated in CI (document why in a comment) but at minimum mock os.rename to raise OSError(errno=EXDEV) to force the copytree fallback path and assert partial-destination cleanup on a subsequent copytree failure.
acceptance_criteria: Each bullet has a passing, meaningful test; fsx module coverage gaps at the listed line numbers closed (except any explicitly documented as unsimulatable).

title: Add resolve.compose 'archetype not in catalog' test
description:
src/python_foundry/resolve/compose.py:38 is uncovered. Existing tests/test_resolve.py only test an archetype TYPE that fails spec-level validation (bypassing resolve entirely). The realistic failure mode -- a spec with a structurally valid archetype string (e.g. 'cli') that is simply absent from the loaded catalog (e.g. a partial/custom catalog tree) -- is never tested at the resolve layer.

Add a test that builds/loads a catalog missing the 'cli' archetype unit (e.g. via a tmp_path catalog tree, or a filtered in-memory catalog if the API supports it) and calls resolve() with a spec whose archetype='cli'; assert ResolveError is raised with the correct code (e.g. resolve.unknown_archetype) and error_class='resolve', and that the message references the missing archetype id.
acceptance_criteria: New test passes and fails if resolve/compose.py:38's check is removed.

title: Test suite hardening: close error-path and edge-case coverage gaps
description:
Follow-up epic from a deep-dive test-quality audit (2026-08-01) covering the
full test suite (tests/*.py) against src/python_foundry/*.

Audit method: three parallel subagent reviews across (1) spec/catalog/resolve/plan
(pure logic layer), (2) fsx/generate/verify/render (orchestration layer), and
(3) cli/report/hybrid (surface layer), each reading source + tests line-by-line
against docs/02-definitive-specification-revised.md.

## Why this exists
Coverage is 85% (139 tests passing) with strong happy-path and a few excellent
spec-critical tests (verify precedence matrix, plan_sha256 test vector, purity
import guard). But there is a systemic pattern: nearly every module's *error
branches* are untested, even where those branches implement explicit spec
requirements (fail-closed writes, closed error taxonomy REQ-091, catalog
integrity, hard-fail unknown keys). hybrid/__main__.py (public template CI
drift gate) has 0% coverage.

## Scope
Child issues below cover, by area:
- Critical: hybrid/__main__.py zero coverage; dead "unknown keys" test;
  verify runner real-failure paths (ruff/ty/pytest never actually triggered);
  catalog integrity checks untested; generate orchestration error branches;
  archetype-not-in-catalog gap.
- High: fsx stage/place error paths; generate/lock.py failure paths;
  render/stage_render.py error paths; CLI JSON failure schema assertions;
  report error_class taxonomy completeness; purity-import guard scope.
- Medium: unicode/edge-case spec input; plan bind artifact load errors;
  digest normalization; plan_text warnings/truncation branches.
- Hygiene: consolidate test_spk101_e2e.py / test_spk102_forbidden.py overlap
  with test_fsx.py / test_ms003a_cli_core.py; strengthen weak assertions
  (e.g. test_load_spec_does_not_write only checks "no exception").
- New testing capability: fault-injection tests for verify tiers (real
  failing ruff/ty/pytest input, not just none-mode); contract test asserting
  every closed error_class is reachable end-to-end via CLI; consider
  hypothesis-based property tests for canonical_json_bytes/plan_sha256.

## Non-goals
- No relaxation of existing product locks (ty, fnox+age, exclusive place,
  closed catalog, etc.)
- Not re-litigating spec requirements; only closing verification gaps against
  the already-accepted spec.

## Acceptance criteria
- All Critical + High child issues closed with passing tests.
- Coverage report shows no module below ~85% except intentionally-excluded
  code (e.g. __main__ dispatch stubs), and hybrid/__main__.py specifically
  covered.
- CI has a coverage gate (tracked separately, see python-foundry-cli coverage
  tooling issue).

title: REQ-059/REQ-061 profile dependencies never actually added to generated pyproject.toml (fixed during review)
description: Root cause (fixed in this session): plan/construct.py hardcoded plan.body['dependencies'] = [] regardless of selected profiles; catalog manifests for profile/http and profile/data-etl carried no 'dependencies' field; core/scripts pyproject.toml.tmpl hardcoded 'dependencies = []'. Net effect: selecting the http or data-etl profile never actually added httpx / polars+pyarrow to the generated project's pyproject.toml, so 'uv sync' would never install them despite REQ-059 ('Profile http MUST add httpx') and REQ-061 ('profile data-etl Default MUST be polars + pyarrow'). The profile stub files (http_client.py.tmpl, etl_utils.py.tmpl) only returned decorative strings and never imported the libraries, so the gap was invisible to any existing test. Fixed: added UnitManifest.dependencies + ResolvedProject.dependencies, merged in resolve/compose.py, threaded through plan/construct.py's dependencies field and render/stage_render.py build_context() as a new 'dependencies_toml' template var used by core + scripts pyproject.toml.tmpl. Updated profiles/http and profiles/data-etl manifests to declare their real dependencies, made the stub files actually import the libraries, removed the now-redundant profiles/http/files/pyproject.profile.http.toml.static placeholder, regenerated the MS-001 golden plan + plan_sha256 test vector (catalog content changed), and added regression tests in tests/test_archetypes_profiles.py covering both profiles end-to-end via generate(run_lock=False, run_verify_tools=False).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting profile=http adds httpx to the generated pyproject.toml dependencies; selecting profile=data-etl adds polars+pyarrow. Without any profile, dependencies stay empty. Full test suite, ruff, and ty all green.
close_reason: Fixed and verified during full-project review session: see bead descriptions for root cause + fix summary. Full suite (137 tests), ruff, and ty all green after each fix.

title: generate: placed project ships broken .venv (stale absolute shebang paths after stage move)
description: Root cause: generate/orchestrate.py runs default/strict verify (uv sync --locked, ruff, ty, pytest) inside the stage directory, which creates .venv with absolute-path console-script shebangs baked to the stage path. exclusive_place() then os.rename()s the stage directory to the final destination. The moved .venv's script shebangs (e.g. .venv/bin/pytest -> #!/abs/stage/path/.venv/bin/python) still point at the old (now-deleted) stage path, so any 'uv run <tool>' in the placed project fails with exec: ... No such file or directory (exit 126) until the user manually re-runs 'uv sync'. This is reproducible today and fails the project's own SPK-001 smoke test (tests/test_spk001_smoke.py::test_spk001_tools_green_on_generated_minimal), which runs 'uv run pytest' etc. immediately after generate() places the project. Violates the spirit of REQ-080 default verify (tooling-sync green) and MS-002 (first successful generate to empty dest with default verify) since the placed project is not actually usable without a hidden manual re-sync step.
acceptance_criteria: After generate() places a project with default or strict verify, running 'uv run pytest', 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ty check' etc. directly in the placed destination succeeds without requiring a prior manual 'uv sync'. tests/test_spk001_smoke.py passes. No stale/broken .venv (or other stage-path-relative build caches) is shipped in the placed project.
close_reason: Fixed and verified during full-project review session: see bead descriptions for root cause + fix summary. Full suite (137 tests), ruff, and ty all green after each fix.

title: P01: Optional --plan bind API shape (no writes)
description:
Implement optional plan-bind API shape without performing stage writes (FND-004).

Must:
- Load --plan JSON plan artifact
- Recompute Construct from current inputs
- Hard-fail with error_class=plan_bind if plan_sha256, foundry version, or catalog digest mismatch
- Fail BEFORE any write/stage API is invoked

REQs: REQ-086 (shape), REQ-024
## Acceptance Criteria
- Match succeeds (API returns bound plan)
- Bit-flipped plan_sha256 fails with plan_bind
- No stage directories created on mismatch
- Unit/integration tests without fsx writes

title: P01: Plan Construct + plan_sha256 canonicalization
description:
Implement pure `plan` package: immutable Generation Plan Construct.

Must include (§9.3):
- foundry version + catalog digest
- normalized spec (profiles membership list)
- resolved archetype + profiles in catalog apply order (kind-qualified)
- planned files (path, mode, render kind, content digest) — stubs OK
- dependencies/pins/lock production intent
- external steps + verify_mode + verify_source
- plan_sha256 over canonical JSON excluding that field
- warnings (non-binding)

Canonicalization (REQ-026 / FND-009):
- UTF-8 JSON, sorted keys every level, compact separators, no NaN/Inf
- SHA-256 lowercase hex of preimage
- Fixed test vector (minimal plan → known hash)
- No wall-clock/random in plan body (RSK-100)

Purity (REQ-082): plan MUST NOT import fsx, generate, or cli.

REQs: REQ-024, REQ-025, REQ-026, REQ-041, REQ-082, REQ-087
## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixed plan_sha256 test vector passes
- Deterministic across repeated runs
- Import-boundary architecture test exists
- Kind-qualified unit refs in plan JSON

title: P01: Resolve archetype + profile set composition

title: PHASE-01 — Pure pipeline (MS-001)
description:
Implement write-free pipeline: parse/validate Project Spec, load closed catalog, resolve archetype+profiles (set membership; catalog apply order), resolve effective verify fields, Construct Generation Plan with plan_sha256 and error_class taxonomy; expose optional --plan bind API shape without stage writes.

title: generate --verify none: loud warning is computed but never surfaced to CLI/API caller
description: Spec §9.5.2 requires verify mode 'none' to produce a loud warning to the user (explicit opt-out, no tool proof). src/python_foundry/verify/runners.py run_verify() already builds VerifyResult(mode='none', skipped=True, warning='verify mode is none: ...') but src/python_foundry/generate/orchestrate.py:generate() calls run_verify(...) and discards the return value entirely (never stored on GenerateResult). src/python_foundry/cli/main.py generate_cmd() has no code path that could show this warning even if it existed on the result. Net effect: running 'foundry generate --verify none' silently skips all tooling proof with zero user-visible warning, violating REQ-080's 'loud warning' requirement. No test exercises 'foundry generate --verify none' end-to-end and asserts a warning is shown.
acceptance_criteria: GenerateResult carries the verify warning (when present) and the CLI (both text and --json output) surfaces it to the user for --verify none. A test exercises generate() and/or the CLI with verify=none and asserts the warning text is present in the result/output.
close_reason: Fixed: GenerateResult now carries verify_warning (populated from run_verify()'s VerifyResult.warning), surfaced in CLI text output (stderr WARNING line) and --json output (verify_warning field). Added tests/test_generate.py::test_generate_verify_none_surfaces_loud_warning and test_generate_cmd_verify_none_prints_warning. Full suite (139 tests), ruff, ty all green.
